findings.issue: The new bullet says 'an attacker cannot renew a lock', and the Victim DoS bullet still says the lock is 'never permanent'. Both are true for a single lock. But failed_attempts is not reset when a lock expires, so one wrong OTP right after expiry re-locks the account at the 15 m maximum straight away. That is about 4 requests an hour, the same as the password path. Security r1 asked for this residual to be stated.
findings.fix: Add a short clause: 'a persistent attacker can re-lock right after each lock expires (same as the password path)'.

findings.issue: The bound is now 1 s (one 250 ms timeout, then the 5 s skip), which makes it a real check. It could still flake on a loaded docker CI host. A context assertion on RedisProperties.getTimeout() (optional in r1) was not added, so removing the YAML timeout still fails no test.
findings.fix: Optional: add a one-line context test asserting spring.data.redis.timeout == 250ms. Loosen to about 2 s if the test flakes.

findings.issue: Uses the fully qualified java.time.Instant inline instead of an import.
Still open from security r1, outside this diff's scope: the add-phone SMS send (POST /api/auth/me/phone) has no per-phone or daily caps, which leaves an SMS-pumping vector.

summary: The delta resolves the main round-1 finding, raised by both reviewer and security. In OtpLoginService.verify (lines 125-133), a wrong code now calls loginAttempts.recordFailure only when !loginAttempts.isLocked(userId), and it still throws AUTH_OTP_INVALID. The response is unchanged, so there is no new oracle, and this matches the password path. The new OtpLockoutIT.wrongOtpsDoNotRenewLock test proves it. It locks the account with 5 wrong OTPs, sends 3 more, and checks that each one still returns AUTH_OTP_INVALID (the wrongOtp helper asserts the error code). It then checks that locked_until and failed_attempts have not changed. Backoff grows with failed_attempts, so without the fix both assertions would fail (5 would become 8 and the lock would move). Unknown, unverified and OTP-only paths are untouched. A race between isLocked and recordFailure can at most add one extra failure, which is benign. The other round-1 items: 'sends' changed to 'requests' in env-descriptions.json, environment-variables.md and auth-service.md, with the cooldown interaction explained; the refresh-capacity text and the stale Bucket4j Javadoc in UserCredential and LoginAttemptService were fixed; the fallback-map wholesale clear and the Redis maxmemory/eviction expectation are now documented as soft controls; the timeout-test bound was tightened from 5 s to 1 s. Still open: the add-phone SMS cap (security r1, out of scope, needs a backlog entry) and the optional RedisProperties timeout context test. Evidence shows forge-verify passing at fca9bc19 with 101 tests and 0 failures. No blocker or major findings; all ACs are still met.
